_what: Act D live-meshing viability: wall-clock of the real mesh pipeline that builds the 38,304-cell grid Act D's numbers belong to.
mesher: pyHyp hyperbolic extrusion from a CGNS surface mesh, then plot3dToFoam / autoPatch / createPatch / renumberMesh. THIS PIPELINE DOES NOT MESH AN STL.
ranks_note: the pipeline is serial; the container was given a 4-core quota, matching how the recorded A2 run was containerised

identity_assert.why: the timing only means anything if the mesh built is the mesh Act D's numbers belong to

mesh_only_definition: untar_done -> renumberMesh_done: coarsen, pyHyp extrusion, plot3dToFoam, autoPatch, createPatch, renumberMesh. Excludes the archive untar and the checkMesh audit.
container_wall_definition: immediately before `docker run` to immediately after it; includes container start and the DAFoam environment source.

cost.cost_basis: dollars DERIVED at the recorded c7a.4xlarge rate $0.0513/core-h, NOT measured; the box cannot read its own billing (COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER.md section 5).

total_in_20_to_300_s.note: FALSIFIED, and recorded as such. The registered band was wrong: the pipeline is an order of magnitude faster than predicted.

verdict_rule: registered before the run: live cell-by-cell meshing on camera is viable only if total mesh wall time <= 60 s (Sanaa's own 'seconds to a minute').
verdict_reading: The real mesher builds Act D's exact 38,304-cell grid in 8.02 s. Live meshing is viable for this act at Sanaa's stated pace, with margin.
what_this_does_NOT_say: This is not a measurement of meshing an STL. The mesher's input is a CGNS surface mesh. Whether snappyHexMesh could build a comparable grid from mach_tutorial_wing.stl, and how long that would take, was not measured and no number for it is reported.

addendum_2026_09_01.what: A caveat on the scope of the verdict. Adds nothing to and removes nothing from the gate, threshold, cap or label registered at 6e911354; those are closed.
addendum_2026_09_01.the_gap: This measured THE MESHER. Sanaa's stage description is 'the real mesher on the uploaded STL, the computational grid drawn cell by cell, wall-layer zoom, slot/wall resolution table'. The 8.021 s covers the mesher only. DRAWING 38,304 cells one at a time in the viewport is a rendering cost in the browser, and it was NOT measured here and is not covered by this PASS.
addendum_2026_09_01.why_it_matters: A cell-by-cell draw of 38,304 cells at, say, 60 frames per second and one cell per frame would take about 10 minutes. The drawing rate is a display choice (cells per frame), not a solver fact, so it is the GUI's to set -- but nobody should read this PASS as saying the whole meshing STAGE fits in 8 seconds. It says the MESH does.
addendum_2026_09_01.what_would_close_it: A measurement of the viewport's own draw rate for this grid, taken by cfd in the GUI pipeline, against whatever cells-per-frame the stage chooses. Not measured by this lane and not estimated here.
